label: Answerability bridge versus goal-relative force for preference-independent epistemic reasons
summary: Ran context/dossier/related on the target. Existing Boundary goalRelative frame already shows F6, consideration presentation and the ordinary-role definition fail to exclude the goal-relative rival; accuracy certificates and the nihilism retorsion bind only subjects already taking a correctness aim. Verified four zero-axiom results: actual-force concession plus belief answerability entail the target; goal-relative force plus an indifference alternative entail its negation (so concession, answerability, goal-relativism and indifference are jointly inconsistent); goal-relative force plus a constitutive aim, composed with ordinaryFromThin, entail the target; finite controls separate every premise of the answerability argument and include an actually indifferent subject whose ordinary reason lacks actual force. Rejected: treating accuracy dominance or retorsion as binding indifferent profiles; an all-attitude answerability (stronger than needed). Provisional judgment proposed: underdetermined, leaning supported; strongest objection is the attributive standard versus reason-giving distinction. Details and warrant assessment in docs/notes/epistemic-authority.md. No root connection; frontier-diff no change.
blocker: Answerability and the constitutive aim remain open bare bridges; no finite frame discriminates attributive correctness from reason-giving force. Root connection needs a statement linking belief-answerable reasons to the case's premise-assessment attitude.
